title: SAP OVERPASS: Critical RCE Vulnerability Exposes Enterprise Secrets, Commands, and Data
content_md:
SAP has patched a critical RCE vulnerability in its kernel, dubbed OVERPASS (CVE-2026-44756). Discovered by Onapsis, the flaw allows bypassing access verification and gaining server control, accessing user data, financial information, and corporate secrets. The vulnerability affects SAP S/4HANA, SAP ERP, Business Suite, NetWeaver Application Server ABAP, Web Dispatcher, BW/4HANA, Enterprise Portal, PI/PO, Solution Manager, and other kernel-based products. Onapsis identified over 10,000 unique IP addresses with internet-accessible SAP web interfaces, calling this estimate conservative.

The vulnerability resides in the kernel code handling the Extended Passport Protocol (EPP). The kernel processes the EPP structure during new session opening, before user authentication. This means account lockouts, complex passwords, roles, and authorization limits cannot prevent the attack. A specially formatted request allows taking control of the process and executing arbitrary OS commands with SAP administrative privileges.

After a successful attack, an attacker can read the SAP Secure Store, extract database access credentials and password hashes, intercept active user session data, and obtain saved credentials for lateral movement between connected SAP systems. Access also allows modifying configuration, applications, and SAP binary files. Possible scenarios include theft of financial and personnel information, modification of vendor banking data, creation of privileged users, backdoor installation, and ransomware deployment.

SAP resolved the vulnerability in the September 2026 security updates, releasing Security Note 3747649. According to Onapsis, the only way to fully eliminate the risk is to update the kernel. Network limits can temporarily reduce the attack surface but cannot protect all interfaces simultaneously, since the vulnerable EPP is processed through multiple protocols before authorization verification.
